newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai non-oil trade up 19 pct in first half.
newsitem.headline: Dubai non-oil trade up 19 pct in first half.

text.p: The value of Dubai's non-oil trade grew 19 percent to 41 billion dirhams ($11 billion) in the first half of 1996 from the same period last year, a report by the English language Khaleej Times newspaper said on Sunday.
The report, quoting Dubai's Department of Ports and Customs, said imports rose 16 percent to 30.7 billion dirhams from 26.4 billion dirhams in the first six months of 1995.
"Non-oil exports declined by 6.5 percent to 2.1 billion dirhams from 2.2 billion dirhams," the report said.
It said China remained the main exporter to Dubai with an estimated 11 percent of Dubai's imports. Exports to Japan accounted for almost 15 percent of Dubai's non-oil exports.
Re-exports showed a growth of 39.6 percent to 8.1 billion dirhams from 5.8 billion dirhams the previous year.
Dubai, a Gulf trade and re-export centre, says its non-oil trade grew by 10 percent in 1995 to 72.4 billion dirhams.
